subject: Specialty insurance exhibit request & PO onboarding
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@brightfoundry.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Initial docs for vendor setup

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks for the warm welcome — excited to get BrightFoundry set up as a Redwood supplier. Per your onboarding checklist the procurement team asked for: 

- Certificate of Insurance (COI) showing General Liability and Workers' Comp
- Cyber liability summary and claims history (last 3 years)
- A list of subcontractors who will process customer data

I've attached the COI and a short cyber summary to this email (see attachment stubs below). The subcontractor list is in progress; Jake is looping in our operations team to finalize it.

Attachments: BrightFoundry_COI_2027.pdf (PDF, 140KB), BrightFoundry_Cyber_Summary.pdf (PDF, 95KB)

Are there any special endorsements Redwood requires (additional insured, waiver of subrogation, primary/noncontributory) for vendors doing model hosting?

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Sr. Procurement Ops
BrightFoundry Inc

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@brightfoundry.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial docs for vendor setup

Hi Lena — welcome. Quick notes and next steps: 

1) Thank you for the COI + cyber summary. We'll need a couple of clarifications before we can start PO provisioning: 
   - COI: does the policy include an Additional Insured endorsement that names "Redwood Inference, its affiliates and customers"? If not, we normally request the insurance broker add a data-processing specific Additional Insured endorsement scoped to activities under the agreement.
   - Cyber: can you confirm retroactive date and whether the policy covers third-party service provider incidents (vendor-originated breach) with at least $2M limit?

2) Subcontractor list: please include which subcontractors will have production access to customer data and whether they are processing within the US or EU. If any subcontractor is in APAC, flag that as well.

3) Upload: we prefer documents in the vendor portal. Upload link: https://vendors.redwoodinfra.com/portal/upload/BRF-1234 — I'll trigger PO provisioning once the attachments and endorsements are clear.

If helpful I can jump on a quick 20-minute call to walk through the endorsement language we need.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Lena Ortiz <lena@brightfoundry.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Jake Moyer <jmoyer@brightfoundry.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 14:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial docs for vendor setup

Karthik — thanks for the breakdown. A few answers below: 

- COI: our carrier can add an Additional Insured endorsement. We typically name the buyer (Redwood) and can add the specific language you mentioned. We do have a primary/noncontributory clause for our commercial general liability (CGL) but waiver of subrogation will require carrier sign-off — I'll confirm.
- Cyber: current retroactive date is 2024-06-01. Limits: $3M per occurrence, includes third-party vendor liability.
- Subcontractors: Jake attached the current list; two partners (DataMesh Ops, EdgeServe) will have limited production access — both US-based.

I'm attaching the subcontractor list now (stubbed). Let me know if we need an endorsement template to share with our broker.

Attachments: BrightFoundry_Subcontractor_List.xlsx (XLSX, 28KB)

Lena

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@brightfoundry.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial docs for vendor setup

Hi Lena — appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of procurement specifics from our side to avoid delays once PO is generated: 

- Endorsement language we need (short version):
  • Additional Insured: "Redwood Inference, its subsidiaries and customers, as their interests may appear" for GL policies related to the contract activities.
  • Primary and Noncontributory: yes for CGL.
  • Waiver of Subrogation: preferred but we can accept conditional approval (carrier confirmation within 5 business days).

- PO terms: Redwood issues a conditional PO while insurance endorsements are processed; the PO will become unconditional once the portal shows the endorsed form and broker confirmation. Expected lead time for your broker's endorsement varies but historically carriers take 3–7 business days.

Ben from Finance is copied to confirm invoicing details and PO numbering. Ben — once we have endorsements confirmed and uploaded, can you queue a provisional PO (PR-2027-BRF-009)?

Short call would help if carrier needs the exact endorsement phrasing — happy to schedule.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Vendor Risk & Procurement
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Lena Ortiz <lena@brightfoundry.com>
Date: Wed, 06 Oct 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial docs for vendor setup

Thanks team — I can confirm Finance will provision PR-2027-BRF-009 (conditional) today. Couple of notes: 

- Please ensure the submitted invoice references the PR number exactly as: PR-2027-BRF-009. That helps AP automation.
- If BrightFoundry plans to issue an advance invoice for mobilization, we require a short schedule of deliverables tied to any advance payment.

I'll leave scheduling to Karthik / Marissa. Lena — if you can upload the endorsed COI plus a broker confirmation email to the vendor portal by EOD tomorrow we'll close the PO as unconditional.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jake Moyer <jmoyer@brightfoundry.com>

We uploaded the updated COI and the broker confirmation stub to your portal link: https://vendors.redwoodinfra.com/portal/upload/BRF-1234 (file names: BrightFoundry_COI_2027_ENDORSED.pdf, BrightFoundry_Broker_Confirm.pdf).
